proposed_statement_changes.reason: The frozen claim uses the refuted widening-polynomial prior, fixed widening schedules, and an obsolete error ledger that are not conclusions of the corrected Airy machine. The replacement drops those unsupported objects and narrows the theorem to the exact corrected Airy diagonal, its four certified errors, and the computable common tail supplied by the unchanged allocation-tube root.

proposed.justification: The explicit error budget turns a limiting theorem into a finite, checkable claim and separates cross-sample convergence from action-grid discretization.
proposed.gap: The accepted parent bounds the two certificates at a selected \(n\) by \(1/(4G^2)\) but gives no computable threshold or allocation-shell modulus linking different population sizes.
proposed.consumer: A protocol designer can certify worst-case precision at a planned sample size from one prespecified sequence of tube widths, truncations, allocation radii, action grids, and rational enclosure widths.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Rewire the target to the unchanged corrected allocation-tube root and the corrected finite-input, Airy-record, and rational-grid evaluator lemmas; remove every obsolete widening-prior dependency and declare the symbols of the corrected certificate.
